programs.nl_rule:
In the input, you should see...3x3 grid

The output grid size...9x9 grid

To make the output, you have to...each tile in the input grid is a 3x3 grid pattern on the output. Keep same color and pattern but increase to a 9x9 grid

content.text:
Let me understand the task. The rule: input 3x3 grid, output 9x9 grid where each cell is upscaled by factor 3 (each value becomes a 3x3 block of same color).

I need to teach the Student. The student hasn't seen my example. I should show examples via show_example or show_transformed_input.

Let me show a couple of examples. Actually the verifier just upscales by factor 3. Let me show the teacher example via show_example? Wait, show_example requires me to author both input and output, and if matches rule, shown. I can just show_transformed_input with various inputs, which auto-generates gold.

Best approach: show_transformed_input with a few diverse inputs to demonstrate the pattern. Let me do a couple with different colors and maybe a full pattern.

Let me show one simple and one more complex. Actually showing the teacher's example directly would be good. I can use show_example with the exact given input/output (which I know matches).

Let me use show_transformed_input for a few inputs. Since verifier just upscales, any 3x3 input works.

Let me show 2-3 examples.

Actually, to teach well, I could show the teacher example via show_example (I have the exact output). And maybe one more distinct example via show_transformed_input. That should be enough. The rule is simple.

Let me do show_example with the given pair, and show_transformed_input with another 3x3.

Then start_exam.

Let me pick a second example input that covers distinct colors, e.g. [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]] -> upscaled. This demonstrates clearly. I'll use show_transformed_input.

Actually maybe I should also query the student to check? Could be helpful. But simple enough. Let me just show two examples and maybe one probe.

I'll do show_example (teacher example) and show_transformed_input in parallel? They're independent. Yes.

Let me call both.

tools.name: show_example

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

output_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Show the Student a labeled input-output pair that you authored. If your output matches the rule, the pair is shown and you receive a success acknowledgement only. If it does not match, the pair is not shown and you receive the gold output so you can correct it.

tools.name: show_transformed_input

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Provide only an input grid. The environment applies the verifier and shows the resulting gold input-output pair to the student.

tools.name: query_student

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Probe the student with an input of your choice. You receive the student's predicted output, the gold output, and whether they matched. The student does not see the gold pair unless you later show it with show_example or show_transformed_input.

tools.name: start_exam
tools.description: End teaching and send the student to the exam: they must solve held-out generator inputs (unseen in demonstrations or probes) with the history so far. No further teaching after this.

content.text: Both shown. The rule is clear: upscale by factor 3. I think two examples suffice. Let me start the exam.
